inputSentence: Nintendo Switch 2 launches worldwide on June 5, 2025.
heroSummary: Nintendo's next console arrives with a larger display, updated social features, and a launch line-up built around the company's biggest franchises. This page packages the launch date, pricing, launch software, and rollout questions editors will keep updating.
whatChanged: Nintendo moved from tease to shipping plan: Switch 2 has a firm release date, flagship launch titles, and a hardware story centered on continuity with the original Switch ecosystem.
whyItMatters: A Nintendo hardware cycle is a cross-desk event. It affects consumer tech, games publishing, retail demand, and the cadence of first-party releases for the next several years.

keyFacts.label: Core hook
keyFacts.value: Switch-style hybrid play with upgraded hardware

timeline.title: Nintendo formally reveals the console
timeline.description: Nintendo confirms the successor name, keeps the hybrid handheld-plus-dock format, and frames compatibility as a central transition strategy.

timeline.title: A dedicated Direct fills in specs and software
timeline.description: Nintendo uses a hardware-focused presentation to disclose launch timing, pricing, first-party support, and a broader software roadmap.

timeline.title: Global retail launch begins
timeline.description: The story shifts from speculation to availability: preorder fulfillment, day-one reviews, and launch-week software performance become the coverage center.

watchItems.title: Supply versus demand
watchItems.description: Editors should watch retailer stock updates, preorder cancellations, and whether Nintendo can keep inventory flowing through the first month.

watchItems.title: Backward compatibility friction
watchItems.description: Compatibility is a selling point, but real-world reporting needs to verify save migration, accessory support, and performance deltas on legacy games.

watchItems.title: Launch-window exclusives
watchItems.description: The early software slate determines whether Switch 2 feels like an immediate must-buy or a more gradual upgrade cycle.

watchItems.title: Price narrative
watchItems.description: The higher starting price changes the consumer framing from toy-like impulse buy to premium hardware purchase.

entities.name: Nintendo
entities.detail: Controls the hardware roadmap, launch messaging, and first-party release cadence that will determine whether the transition feels clean.

entities.name: Mario Kart World
entities.detail: Acts as the broadest mainstream software proof point for the new system and a reason for households to upgrade early.

entities.name: Retail partners
entities.detail: Big-box chains and online storefronts will show whether launch allocation is meeting consumer demand.

coverageAngles.title: Is this a true generational leap?
coverageAngles.description: Compare the system's real-world performance and industrial design against the original Switch rather than relying on spec sheets alone.

coverageAngles.title: How sticky is Nintendo's ecosystem?
coverageAngles.description: Track how Nintendo balances continuity with the need to create exclusives that justify new hardware.

coverageAngles.title: What does the price say about the market?
coverageAngles.description: The launch sits inside a more expensive consumer-electronics cycle, so pricing becomes a macro as well as product story.

coverageAngles.title: Who gets left behind?
coverageAngles.description: Look at owners of the original Switch, Lite, and OLED models and which groups still have little reason to upgrade immediately.

faq.question: What is the one-sentence story?
faq.answer: Nintendo has put a date, price, and launch line-up around its next console, turning abstract anticipation into a concrete retail event.

faq.question: Why does a topic page help here?
faq.answer: Hardware launches generate fragmented updates across announcements, accessories, retail, reviews, and software. A topic page keeps those threads in one surface.

faq.question: What changes after launch day?
faq.answer: The page becomes less about promised features and more about verified availability, reception, and whether the software pipeline sustains momentum.
